LESSON: CLASSES OF FIRE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Mixtures, Elements and Compounds
Topic 1.3: Classes of fire
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Classes of fire, part of Mixtures, Elements and Compounds in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 INTEGRATED SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why are fires a danger in nature?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss the possible causes of fire in nature and share. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication during the discussion.

2. Discuss the role of the fire triangle in the spread of fire and present in class. Learners with speech difficulties could also use residual speech as they are lip read by peers or

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss the possible causes of fire in nature and share. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication during the discussion.
2. Discuss the role of the fire triangle in the spread of fire and present in class. Learners with speech difficulties could also use residual speech as they are lip read by peers or

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Classes of fire together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: The learner enhances active community life skills by making posters on classes of fires and their control

measures and hanging them at the places where they can be seen.

● Communication and collaboration: The learner acquires listening, speaking and recording skills as they discusses the

causes of fire, dangers of fire and rights to safety

Values:
● Respect: The learner observes rules of engagement while working with peers to classify fire according to the cause and

suggest control measures.

● Responsibility: The learner accommodates each other’s views and opinions as they discuss rights to safety information on

flammable substances.

Link to other Learning areas:

The learner practices safety measures to prevent fire accidents in nature as a life skill in Social studies.
